group_assessment.counts_measured: Not measured, declared as not measured. Aqeilan and Croce at Ohio State with Marius Sudol, who is the WW-domain field itself — refs 16, 17, 22 of this article are his, and the WW-domain nomenclature and the YAP-as-proline-rich-ligand-binder characterisation are his work.
group_assessment.weighting: The observation is authoritative and the co-authorship is the reason: the competition experiment is a WW-domain experiment designed with the person who defined the domain class. The interpretation is where care is owed, and the authors themselves show it — the conclusion is written 'may compete', and the model figure is labelled 'a proposed model'. The over-reach in this corpus has never been theirs; it has been in how the frame was carried forward.

three_arcs_kept_separate.why: The authorisation requires it, and the requirement is not bureaucratic: a single sentence in a later paper compresses two provenances, and compression is how a hedged result becomes a fact.
three_arcs_kept_separate.arc_1_this_article: DATO — WWOX and YAP compete for interaction with ErbB-4, via WWOX's first WW domain, demonstrated by a YAP2 titration co-IP and a Y33R rescue. The authors state it as 'may compete'; this manifest states it as they did. Generalised by the authors to 'PPxY-containing target proteins' as a class, with p73 and AP-2γ named in the model.
three_arcs_kept_separate.arc_2_pmid_23370280: DATO of a DIFFERENT source — WWOX competes with ITCH on ΔNp63α, shown there by direct co-immunoprecipitation with a WWOX-Y33R rescue control. That evidence is primary to Salah 2013 and is NOT retro-attributable here. The reading of 23370280 in this corpus is partial_fulltext_read, which does not license a global characterisation of that paper.
three_arcs_kept_separate.arc_3_the_combination: INFERENZA, and it belongs to neither paper alone — that a therapeutic lever on the WW/ITCH interaction network risks non-selective effects. It requires both arcs and is supported by neither on its own.
three_arcs_kept_separate.🔴 what_this_adjudication_does_not_do: It does not make 'ITCH is not selective' a DATO of PMID 16061658, and it does not make this article the primary evidence for any WWOX–ITCH interaction. The sentence in Salah 2013 that reads 'compete with other WW domain-containing proteins, like YAP and ITCH' is a back-reference for the YAP half and a forward-claim on their own data for the ITCH half; each proposition goes to the source that measured it.

entries.proposition: THE PREMISE THE EXPERIMENT TESTS, IN THE AUTHORS' OWN WORDS. Both proteins carry tandem class-I WW domains and both bind PPxY ligands; the hypothesis is that they therefore contend for the same partners with opposite transcriptional consequences. Adjudicated because a competition result without its hypothesis reads as a discovery about ErbB-4 rather than about WW-domain economy.
entries.snippet: Because WWOX and YAP have the similar tandems of WW domains and interact with common protein targets but have different effects on transactivation, we decided to investigate whether WWOX and YAP expression have opposite effects on their target proteins.
entries.anchor: page 2, end of the Introduction, immediately before Materials and Methods
entries.found_or_sought: sought — the perimeter was decided by looking, and the hypothesis sentence was the first thing the pages showed that the withdrawn keyword perimeter had excluded

entries.proposition: 🔴 THE WW1 ANCHOR. Competition 'at the first WW domain' is asserted throughout the downstream literature and this is where it is established: the Y33R point mutation, which abolishes WWOX binding to p73 and AP2γ, also abolishes binding to ErbB-4.
entries.snippet: These results indicate that the first WW domain of WWOX is primarily responsible for the interaction with ErbB-4.
entries.anchor: page 3, Results, 'WWOX associates physically with ErbB-4', describing Figure 2A lanes 5 and 7
entries.found_or_sought: sought — without it, every downstream 'competition at WW1' is unanchored

entries.proposition: 🔴 THE DATO, FIRST DIRECTION OF THE TITRATION. With YAP2 low, ErbB-4 comes down with WWOX and not with YAP.
entries.snippet: Our results show that in the presence of reduced amount of YAP2, ErbB-4 interacts exclusively with WWOX (Fig. 5A, lane 4 versus 5).
entries.anchor: page 7, Results, 'WWOX and YAP compete for interaction with ErbB-4'
entries.found_or_sought: sought — this is the sentence the authorisation was granted to recover

entries.proposition: THE SECOND DIRECTION, AND THE PART THAT KEEPS THE RESULT HONEST. Raising YAP2 buys YAP some ErbB-4, but WWOX still holds the majority. The competition is real and it is ASYMMETRIC; it is not a switch.
entries.snippet: On the other hand, increased expression of YAP2 causes some ErbB-4-YAP2 association, although ErbB-4-WWOX interaction was still the predominant complex (Fig. 5A, lane 9 versus 8).
entries.anchor: page 7, the sentence immediately following entries[2]

entries.proposition: 🔴 THE CONTROL THAT MAKES IT COMPETITION RATHER THAN CORRELATION. Break WWOX's first WW domain and YAP recovers access to ErbB-4. A point mutation restoring the rival's binding is the strongest form this experiment can take.
entries.snippet: expression of Myc-WWOXY33R resulted in significant rescue of ErbB-4-YAP2 interaction (Fig. 5B, lane 9 versus 8).
entries.anchor: page 7, the Y33R arm of the same paragraph
entries.found_or_sought: sought — the rescue is what separates competition from co-occurrence, and PMID 23370280 uses the identical control on a different partner

entries.proposition: 🔴 AND THE CONCLUSION IS HEDGED IN THE ORIGINAL. The authors write 'may compete'. Every downstream restatement in this corpus should carry that modal, because the paper's own claim is that the data are consistent with competition and that WWOX's occupancy is the prevalent one — not that competition is demonstrated to the exclusion of alternatives.

entries.proposition: PANEL 5A AND 5B, READ AT THE MEASURED CEILING. The blots carry the DATO and they show what the text says, including the asymmetry: at low YAP2 the anti-Omni lane is empty while the anti-WWOX lane is strong; at high YAP2 the anti-Omni lane acquires a faint band while anti-WWOX stays strong; and with Y33R the anti-WWOX lane goes blank while the anti-Omni lane becomes strong. The Y33R arm is the cleanest of the three: the rival gains exactly what the mutant loses.

entries.proposition: WHY THE COMPETITION IS ASYMMETRIC, WHICH IS THE MECHANISM BEHIND 'PREVALENT'. WWOX engages BOTH PPxY motifs of ErbB-4; YAP engages only the COOH-terminal one. A competitor with two contacts against one is not merely a competitor — it is the default occupant, which is exactly what the titration showed.

entries.proposition: 🔴 THE MODEL DIAGRAM, ADJUDICATED FOR AN ABSENCE — AND THE ABSENCE IS READ, NOT COUNTED. Figure 6 draws WWOX bound to an octagon labelled 'Other PPxY-containing partners', to AP2γ and to P73, each with a cross barring the arrow into the nucleus, while YAP carries CTF and P73 through. ITCH APPEARS NOWHERE. This matters because a term count on the refused text layer had returned ITCH = 0 and that zero was correctly withdrawn as NOT_FOUND_IN_TRIAGE: a zero from a surface that mangles printable characters is not evidence of absence. This one comes from a vector diagram rendered at 400 dpi on a page carrying no raster, which is the only kind of zero this article can support. CONSEQUENCE, stated as scope and not as a result: PMID 16061658 anchors WWOX/YAP competition and the PPxY class generalisation, and it is NOT the primary evidence for any WWOX–ITCH claim.
entries.snippet: [figure attestation - pixels cannot be quote-matched] Figure 6, proposed model. A boxed cytoplasm containing ErbB-4 at the membrane with TPA acting through PKC and heregulin binding, γ-secretase releasing CTF. Down the left margin, three black WWOX wedges: one bound to a white octagon reading 'Other PPxY-containing partners', one bound to a grey circle 'AP2γ', one bound to a grey circle 'P73'; the AP2γ and P73 complexes each have an arrow toward the nucleus struck through with a cross. Centre, WWOX bound to CTF with its arrow to the nucleus also crossed, beside an uncrossed CTF that reaches the nuclear oval. Inside the oval, CTF-YAP and P73-YAP drive TRANSCRIPTION. No element of the diagram is labelled ITCH.

That is a `panel_qualifies_text` relation and it was written as one, and the validator refused it — correctly, on its own terms: `qualifies` must point at a TEXT surface, and on a page-adjudicated article there are none, because rule 5e makes every locator a page crop with surface 'figure'. So the relation is recorded in words here instead of as a machine-checkable pointer. It is a real limitation and it is not mine to fix in a manifest: PMID 17803050, the only other fully adjudicated article in this corpus, carries 32 entries all with surface 'figure' and NOT ONE cross-entry relation — the same collapse, unremarked.
